_thresholds: 0 means the defect must not exist. A non-zero ceiling is measured debt, not a target: it exists so a regression fails today, and it should be ratcheted down as the debt is paid. `null` disables a rule (report-only). Re-measure with: node refs/harness/lint.mjs --suggest
_exempt: Selector fragments whose findings are subtracted from a rule's count. This is the only sanctioned way to forgive a defect: it names what is forgiven, in writing, and the audit still reports it in full. Raising a ceiling instead would hide the next, different defect underneath the same number. Deliberately empty — see _standingDecision.
_standingDecision: Decided 2026-07-28, after looking rather than inferring. The slab's 27 clipped and 6 sliced findings at 390x844 are forgiven, and only inside .product-slab-module__*. Reason: the slab is a 480px window onto a full library UI, which is unmistakably wider than a phone, and the mobile repair added a horizontal mask so content dissolves into the ground before the viewport edge instead of terminating against it. Captured the right 150px of the slab at device-scale 3 and confirmed by eye: 'database', 'test' and 'caught' all fade to nothing; no glyph ends on a hard line. That is the whole difference between the defect the owner found (chips ending at 500px against a hard edge, in a section with no window reading at all) and a designed crop. The harness cannot see this distinction — it measures geometry, not perception — which is why the call is recorded here instead of buried in a raised ceiling. Residual risk, stated so the next person inherits it: if the mask is ever removed the geometry will not change, so this exemption would keep the gate green over a real defect. If you touch product-slab.module.css's mask-image, re-verify the right edge by eye and update this note.
